thread.title: The global dominators you invest in when Apple and the chips are down - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: The global dominators you invest in when Apple and the chips are down - MarketWatch
text:
One would think that Apple CEO Tim Cook couldn’t depress the faithful any further after his lead-balloon revenue warning at the start of the year.
But it has been a veritable “school of hard knocks” for investors lately, with Nvidia NVDA, -2.87% sending our dreams of cloud riches up in smoke and widely held Caterpillar CAT, +2.03% bulldozing its way across retirement funds (but hey, it’s only a quarter). So, no doubt some of us (especially in subzero Midwestern locales) will be watching Apple results from under the covers.
$AAPL warned, $INTC warned, $NVDA warned, $CAT warned, $FDX warned. Please let me know the bullish points
— The_Real_Fly (@The_Real_Fly) January 28, 2019 Obviously, Apple’s AAPL, -0.26% forward guidance will prove a big deal today, but others say average selling prices, which came in at $793 when last reported in November, could also be something to watch.
Read: An earnings tsunami — with 113 S&P 500 components — marks ‘pivot point’ for stock market
“A sharp drop here would suggest that demand for the more expensive models is slowing sharply and that peak iPhone or Apple fatigue is creeping in as consumers tire of the incessant minor upgrades, and lack of innovation elsewhere,” CMC Market’s chief market analyst Michael Hewson told clients.
Apple may still have a trick or two up its sleeve, but forget about the glory-gadget days, says Ross Gerber, co-founder and CEO of Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management, who ventures some optimism in our call of the day .
“I think there is upside now because the stock has moved down to what we think to a valuation that doesn’t account for the long-term cash flow potential and as well as the real growth of their services business,” Gerber told Bloomberg News in a recent interview.
“It’s clear that Apple as a product company has reached its maximum potential, but as a services company, it’s in inning two or three. If Apple does anything bold here in services instead of just sticking its little toe in, I think they could make a big impact and grow the business substantially even more so than today,” he said.
Sure, but the faithful should take note that this implies a bit more patience, because he thinks the company will continue taking its lumps over its bigger dealings with China as the trade war plays out.
Gerber says investors who want to avoid the U.S. vs. China mess, have even more reason to seek out the four or five companies with massive monopoly power over their respective businesses, and which can’t even get past Beijing’s regulatory gatekeepers.
The dominance of companies like Amazon AMZN, -2.11% and Alphabet’s Google GOOGL, -1.08% and Netflix NFLX, -1.88% really can’t be altered too much without serious government intervention, he says. “As this continues without any interference, we expect these companies to continue to grow profits and users, and this could go on for a long long time,” says Gerberg.
There is regulatory risk to these companies, but from Europe and not from the U.S., which has proven weaker at lowering the boom, he says, adding: “As an investor, you’ve gotta own these companies for the long term at this point.”
The market The Dow DJIA, +0.13% S&P 500 SPX, -0.28% and Nasdaq COMP, -0.77% are struggling in early trading. See Market Snapshot for more updates.
Gold US:GCU8 and crude oil US:CLU8 are up some, but the dollar DXY, +0.06% is flat. Watch the pound GBPUSD, +0.0152% ahead of key votes on a series of amendments to U.K. PM Theresa May’s Brexit plan.
Europe stocks SXXP, +1.20% are up, while Asia finished mostly lower.
The chart While this is no news flash to parents of adolescents, your teen’s presence on Facebook is fading. Our chart of the day , from U.K. media regulator Ofcom shows that 72% of the 12 to 15-year old set were using Facebook in 2018, versus 74% in 2017 and nearly 100% in 2011.
Facebook-owned Instagram, meanwhile, charged up to 23% from 14% in 2017, while Spotify SPOT, -1.60% and WhatsApp also saw a nice bump.
Here’s another chart that shows 69% of 12 to 15 year-olds have a social-media profile. And, 18% of eight-to-11-year-olds have one, even if most sites won’t allow it. And of the 2,000 U.K. three to 15-year-olds, 89% are regular watchers of YouTube.
The buzz Apple AAPL, -0.26% is scrambling to fix a glitch that lets FaceTime callers listen in on the recipient’s conversation. Speaking of, we’ll get Apple results after the close Tuesday, and analysts say don’t expect fireworks.
Earnings previews: Alibaba , AMD , GE
Pfizer PFE, +1.53% Harley-Davidson HOG, -5.65% Allergan AGN, -7.49% and Rambus RMBS, -5.33% are all down on disappointing results. Xerox XRX, +9.05% XRX, +9.05% and Corning GLW, +9.95% are bucking that trend. Amgen AMGN, -0.04% eBay EBAY, -0.75% and AMD AMD, -3.07% will report after the close.

China’s Huawei has denied any wrongdoings after the U.S. filed charges against the tech company Monday, and some are worried it may complicate this week’s already tough trade talks .
PG&E PCG, +11.74% has officially filed for bankruptcy under chapter 11, and is trying to access $5.5 billion in debtor-in-possession financing to keep going.
CBS CBS, -0.04% says it will air a POTUS interview just ahead of the Super Bowl.
The Quote: Bloomberg Schultz isn’t trying to win the ‘Twitter primary’ “I’m not going to respond to that. It’s childish. I’m not trying to win the Twitter primary.” — That was former Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz who may be eyeing a 2020 presidential run, but who hasn’t exactly been warmly welcomed by any side . He was responding via a CNBC interview to a Monday Twitter taunt by POTUS, who said the former coffee executive didn’t “have the ‘guts’” to run.
The economy Advance trade in goods, Case-Shiller house prices and consumer confidence data are all headed our way. Tuesday also kicks off the two-day Fed meeting. (See a preview here )
